title: Restriction compatibility for the right adjoint of a proper flat pushforward
statement: Let g:Y'\to Y be a morphism of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let f:X\to Y be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], and of finite presentation. Form X'=X\times_Y Y' with g_X:X'\to X and f':X'\to Y' [def-pc-fibre-product], and let a and a' be the right adjoints to Rf_* and Rf'_* on quasi-coherent derived categories [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-derived-direct-image]. For a quasi-compact open immersion j:V\hookrightarrow Y, let f_V:X\times_YV\to V be the base change, let a_V be its right adjoint, and let j_X:X\times_YV\to X be the projection. Then j_X^*a(K)\to a_V(Lj^*K) is an isomorphism for every K in D_QCoh(Y). For a quasi-compact open immersion j':V'\hookrightarrow Y', let f'_{V'}:X'\times_{Y'}V'\to V' be the base change, let a'_{V'} be its right adjoint, and let j'_{X'}:X'\times_{Y'}V'\to X' be the projection. Then j'_{X'}{}^*a'(K')\to a'_{V'}(Lj'^*K') is an isomorphism for every K' in D_QCoh(Y'). Consequently, in the cartesian square above, formation of both right adjoints and of the base-change map is compatible with restriction to quasi-compact opens on either base.

proof.text: For a quasi-compact open V in the base, [lem-sc-right-adjoint-open-support-criterion] gives the equivalence between support preservation for all bounded-below Q supported on Y\setminus V and the restriction map j_X^*a(K) \to a_V(Lj^*K) being an isomorphism for all bounded-below K. The same node's unbounded clause applies once a commutes with direct sums, and [lem-sc-proper-flat-right-adjoint-direct-sums] supplies that hypothesis; hence the equivalence holds for all Q and K in D_QCoh.

The hypotheses on f are proper, flat, and of finite presentation, so [lem-sc-proper-flat-right-adjoint-open-support] gives support preservation for every bounded-below Q supported on Y\setminus V. Applying Step 1, including its direct-sum clause, therefore gives the first restriction isomorphism j_X^*a(K) \to a_V(Lj^*K) for every K in D_QCoh(Y).

The base change f':X'\to Y' is again proper, flat, and of finite presentation by stability under base change: properness is supplied by [lem-pc-proper-base-change], flatness by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change], and finite presentation by part (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. Repeating Steps 1 and 2 for f' and any quasi-compact open V' in Y' gives j'_{X'}{}^*a'(K') \to a'_{V'}(Lj'^*K') as an isomorphism. The base-change transformation is defined by composing the same adjunction unit and counit maps for these open squares; naturality of units, counits, and pullback identifies its restriction with the corresponding restricted base-change transformation. Thus formation of the base-change map is compatible with restriction on either base.
